questions.question: Where should the Lean 4 proofs for BK-435 live?

options.label: sdd/formal/lean/ (Recommended)
options.description: Sits next to alloy/ and tla/, gets one new row in the formal README's layer table. A Lake project (lakefile + lean-toolchain) inside that folder.

options.label: sdd/research/lean-store-model/
options.description: Kept beside the research doc as a research artifact, like the frozen TLA PoC. Signals it is not a maintained layer, but then L1..L6 never become a live gate.

questions.question: How should the Lean toolchain be set up?

options.label: Native-first + Docker (Recommended)
options.description: Same shape as Alloy: scripts/lean_check.sh uses a pinned native `lake` (installed with elan, user-local) and falls back to a pinned Docker image; `hatch run verify-lean`; session-init installs it in containers. Pin v4.34.1 (2026-09-24, settled). Downloads from GitHub work here.

options.label: Docker only
options.description: Only a pinned image and a script. Less to document, but no fast local edit-and-check loop and no editor integration.

options.label: Native only (elan)
options.description: lean-toolchain file + README steps, no Docker fallback. Smallest setup, but an agent container without elan cannot check it.

questions.question: Mathlib, or Lean core only?

options.label: Core only (Recommended)
options.description: No dependency to download or pin beyond Lean itself. AX-6 is a small hand-defined inductive chain; L3's split-of-join lemma on strings is proved by hand (a few dozen lines). Builds in seconds.

options.label: Mathlib
options.description: Brings Relation.ReflTransGen and List/String lemmas, so the proofs are shorter. Cost: a multi-GB cache, a Mathlib commit pin that must match the toolchain, and a slower build. Network via GitHub/Azure blob; not tested through Zscaler.

questions.question: Is L6 (trie correspondence, up to isomorphism) part of this step?

options.label: L1..L5 + D1 now, L6 later (Recommended)
options.description: This step proves what the doc derives in §4 and §7 except L6, over the unrestricted universe. L6 (building the iso to prefix-closed name-sequence sets, both directions) becomes its own step on a later branch.

options.label: All of L1..L6 now
options.description: One branch closes all of §7. L6 is much larger than the rest together, and it also forces deciding what 'isomorphism' preserves (F/I typing, names), which the doc leaves informal.

options.label: L6 stated, proved later
options.description: State L6 as a Lean definition plus a `sorry`-free statement only in a comment, prove L1..L5 now. Fixes the shape of L6 early without the proof cost.

questions.question: The tooling review found that installing Lean in session-init costs a 580 MB download plus a 2.9 GB extract on every claude.ai/code container start (containers are fresh each session). It blocks session start and can use up the hook's time budget before the gh install that runs after it. What should session-init do for Lean?

options.label: Message only (Recommended)
options.description: Session-init prints how to run the check (Docker fallback, or the README's elan setup) and installs nothing. Session start stays fast; a container session that needs Lean installs it on demand. The Local toolchain row says 'no auto-install'.

options.label: Keep the install, run it last
options.description: Keep the auto-install (now hardened), but move it after the gh block so a timeout cannot starve gh. Every container session still pays the download and extract at start.

options.label: Install in the background
options.description: Start the download and extract detached, so session start is not blocked. More code in the hook, and an early `lean_check.sh` run in that session may race a half-finished install (it then falls back to Docker or fails).

questions.question: The axioms are now proved (Lean) and checked (Alloy). Should they become a normative spec, and where?

options.label: Decide later, keep BK-435 open (Recommended)
options.description: Leave the doc as accepted research. Promote once the operations pass (Dafny) or RFC-0021's encodings (BK-434) need a normative base, so the spec is written against a real consumer. BK-435 stays the umbrella; nothing else changes now.

options.label: New spec, e.g. 051-store-model
options.description: Copy AX-1..AX-8 and D1/L1..L6 into a new spec with spec IDs, linking to the Lean/Alloy files as proof. The research doc becomes background. Brings spec-ID and mark-traceability duties (check_spec_marks), with no Python tests yet to cite them.

options.label: Fold into 004-path-model
options.description: Add the axioms as the structure behind the existing path model. Fewer files, but 004 governs runtime path handling across backends, and the axioms deliberately leave out navigation and backends, which mixes two layers.

options.label: Close BK-435, file a follow-up
options.description: Treat machine-checking as BK-435's whole scope, close it now, and file a new backlog item for the promotion question with its own dossier.

questions.question: The trace's `review:` block needs a PR number (`hatch run ship-report <PR> --trace-block-only`). How should a PR for this branch come about?

options.label: You open it, same as before (Recommended)
options.description: You push and open the PR from your side, as you did for store-model-axioms (commits are unsigned; they get re-signed on your private machine). I add the review block once the PR's review has converged.

options.label: Stack onto the Alloy PR
options.description: Combine with bk-435-alloy-store-model into one PR, so there is one review and one review: block for both steps. Means the Alloy trace and this trace are closed out together.

options.label: No PR yet
options.description: Leave the branch pushed only. The review: block stays owed and the trace stays incomplete until a PR exists.

questions.question: The native Lean path (elan + the README steps) is untested on this machine. Test it?

options.label: You test it yourself (Recommended)
options.description: You run the README's elan block yourself (user-local, about 3 GB under ~/.elan) and then `hatch run verify-lean`. I make no install on your machine, same as with Alloy.

options.label: I install elan here and test
options.description: I run the README block in this session (user-local under ~/.elan, no root), confirm `lean_check.sh` takes the native branch, and fix any README gap. Costs about 3 GB of disk and a few minutes of download.

options.label: Leave untested, document it
options.description: Add one line to the README that the native path is untested, and move on. Docker remains the known-good path.
